Every cell below runs when the documentation is built, including the ones that raise.

```{python}
from importlib import resources

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

import pyfixest as pf

data = pf.get_data(N=1000, seed=1234).dropna()
data["Y_binary"] = (data["Y"] > data["Y"].median()).astype(int)
pois = pf.get_data(N=1000, seed=1234, model="Fepois").dropna()

# multi-cohort panel bundled with PyFixest, subset to 200 units
panel = pd.read_csv(
    resources.files("pyfixest.did.data").joinpath("df_het.csv")
).query("unit <= 200")
```

## Core API

Four estimation functions cover the package; see [A first Regression with PyFixest](getting-started.qmd).

```{python}
pf.etable(
    [
        pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2", data=data),
        pf.fepois("Y ~ X1 | f1", data=pois),
        pf.feglm("Y_binary ~ X1 | f1", data=data, family="logit"),
        pf.quantreg("Y ~ X1 + X2", data=data, quantile=0.5),
    ],
    model_heads=["feols", "fepois", "feglm(logit)", "quantreg(0.5)"],
)
```

## Formula grammar

A formula has up to three `|`-separated parts; see [Formula Syntax](tutorials/formula-syntax.qmd).

```{python}
# fixed effects with +, interacted fixed effects with :
pf.etable([pf.feols("Y ~ X1 | f1 + f2", data=data),
           pf.feols("Y ~ X1 | f1:f2", data=data)])
```

```{python}
# IV: a "[endogenous ~ instruments]" term on the right-hand side
# (the fixest-style "Y ~ X2 | f1 | X1 ~ Z1" still works but is deprecated)
pf.feols("Y ~ X2 + [X1 ~ Z1] | f1", data=data).tidy()
```

```{python}
# i(cat) expands a categorical, ref drops a level, i(cat, x) gives slopes on x
pf.etable([pf.feols("Y ~ i(f1, ref=1.0)", data=data),
           pf.feols("Y ~ i(f1, X2)", data=data)], keep=["f1"])
```

```{python}
# X1 * X2 expands to X1 + X2 + X1:X2, X1:X2 is the interaction alone
pf.etable([pf.feols("Y ~ X1 * X2", data=data),
           pf.feols("Y ~ X1:X2", data=data)])
```

```{python}
# sw() over the dependent variables gives one estimation each
pf.feols("sw(Y, Y2) ~ X1", data=data).tidy()
```

## Multiple estimation

Stepwise operators and `split` turn one call into many fits; see [Formula Syntax](tutorials/formula-syntax.qmd).

```{python}
def expansion(fml):
    fits = pf.feols(fml, data=data).tidy().index.get_level_values("fml")
    return " | ".join(fits.unique().tolist())


operators = ["Y ~ X1 + sw(X2, f3)", "Y ~ X1 + sw0(X2, f3)", "Y ~ csw(X1, X2)",
             "Y ~ csw0(X1, X2)", "Y ~ mvsw(X1, X2)"]
pd.DataFrame({"formula": operators, "expands to": [expansion(f) for f in operators]})
```

```{python}
# split fits one model per subsample, fsplit adds the full sample
pf.etable(pf.feols("Y ~ X1", data=data, fsplit="f3"))
```

```{python}
pf.feols("Y ~ csw(X1, X2)", data=data).summary()
```

## Standard errors

Set `vcov` at estimation time or afterwards; see [Standard Errors & Inference](tutorials/standard-errors.qmd).

```{python}
spellings = {
    "iid": "iid", "hetero": "hetero", "HC1": "HC1", "HC2": "HC2", "HC3": "HC3",
    "CRV1": {"CRV1": "f1"}, "CRV3": {"CRV3": "f1"},
    "CRV1 two-way": {"CRV1": "f1 + f2"},
}
pd.DataFrame(
    {k: pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2", data=data, vcov=v).se() for k, v in spellings.items()}
)
```

```{python}
# NW and DK need vcov_kwargs with time_id; DK also needs panel_id; NW without
# panel_id treats the data as one time series and then needs lag and unique
# time values
hac_kwargs = {"time_id": "year", "panel_id": "unit"}
pd.DataFrame(
    {
        hac: pf.feols(
            "dep_var ~ treat", data=panel, vcov=hac, vcov_kwargs=hac_kwargs
        ).se()
        for hac in ["NW", "DK"]
    }
)
```

```{python}
# change inference after estimation, and adjust the small-sample correction
fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 | f1", data=data)
no_ssc = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 | f1", data=data, ssc=pf.ssc(k_adj=False, G_adj=False))
pd.DataFrame({"default": fit.se(), "post-hoc CRV1": fit.vcov({"CRV1": "f1"}).se(),
              "ssc(k_adj=False)": no_ssc.se()})
```

The cells that raise are pinned by `test_cheatsheet_unsupported_combinations` in `tests/test_errors.py`.

```{python}
#| error: true
# HC2 and HC3 are unavailable once fixed effects are absorbed
pf.feols("Y ~ X1 | f1", data=data, vcov="HC2")
```

```{python}
#| error: true
# CRV3 is unavailable for IV models
pf.feols("Y ~ 1 + [X1 ~ Z1]", data=data, vcov={"CRV3": "f1"})
```

```{python}
#| error: true
# quantile regression clusters on one variable only
pf.quantreg("Y ~ X1", data=data, quantile=0.5, vcov={"CRV1": "f1 + f2"})
```

## Post-estimation

The accessors below are shown on an OLS fit. Other estimators inherit them, but not every method is supported; check the support table in [Standard Errors & Inference](tutorials/standard-errors.qmd) before using `ritest()` or `wildboottest()` on anything but `feols`. See [`Feols`](reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.qmd) for the full list.

```{python}
fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1", data=data, vcov={"CRV1": "f1"})
fit.tidy()
```

```{python}
# the same numbers, column by column
stats = {"coef": fit.coef(), "se": fit.se(), "t": fit.tstat(), "p": fit.pvalue()}
pd.DataFrame(stats).join(fit.confint())
```

```{python}
pd.DataFrame({"predict": fit.predict(newdata=data.head(5)), "resid": fit.resid()[:5]})
```

```{python}
fit.fixef().head(3)
```

```{python}
pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2", data=data).wald_test()
```

```{python}
fit.wildboottest(param="X1", reps=99, seed=1234)
```

```{python}
pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2", data=data).ritest(resampvar="X1", reps=99)
```

```{python}
pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2", data=data).decompose(param="X1", reps=99, seed=1234)
```

```{python}
# Sherman-Morrison coefficient update for one new observation
pf.feols("Y ~ X1", data=data.head(900)).update(
    X_new=np.array([[1.0, 0.5]]), y_new=np.array([1.0])
)
```

```{python}
savi = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2", data=data, vcov="hetero")
pd.DataFrame({"evalue": savi.evalue(), "pvalue_savi": savi.pvalue_savi()})
```

```{python}
#| error: true
# the wild cluster bootstrap is OLS-only
pf.fepois("Y ~ X1 | f1", data=pois).wildboottest(param="X1", reps=99, seed=1234)
```

```{python}
#| error: true
# one endogenous variable per model
pf.feols("Y ~ 1 + [X1 + X2 ~ Z1 + Z2]", data=data)
```

## Difference-in-differences

Each estimator takes a long panel with a cohort column; see [Difference-in-Differences Estimation](tutorials/difference-in-differences.qmd).

```{python}
pf.panelview(panel, unit="unit", time="year", treat="treat",
             collapse_to_cohort=True, sort_by_timing=True, figsize=(6, 3))
```

```{python}
es_args = dict(data=panel, yname="dep_var", idname="unit", tname="year", gname="g")
pf.event_study(**es_args).tidy()
```

```{python}
# estimator="saturated" returns a SaturatedEventStudy with cohort-specific effects
saturated = pf.event_study(**es_args, estimator="saturated")
saturated.aggregate().head(3)
```

```{python}
pf.did2s(panel, yname="dep_var", first_stage="~ 0 | unit + year",
         second_stage="~ i(rel_year, ref=-1.0)", treatment="treat",
         cluster="state").tidy().head(3)
```

```{python}
pf.lpdid(**es_args, vcov={"CRV1": "state"}, att=True).tidy()
```

## Plots

`coefplot` plots any coefficients, `iplot` the ones `i()` created; see [Regression Tables](tutorials/regression-tables.qmd).

```{python}
pf.coefplot([pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2", data=data),
             pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1", data=data)], keep="X", coord_flip=False)
```

```{python}
pf.iplot(pf.feols("dep_var ~ i(rel_year, ref=-1.0)", data=panel),
         coord_flip=False, figsize=(9, 3))
```

## Multiple testing

All three take a set of models and one shared parameter; see [`rwolf()`](reference/estimation.post_estimation.multcomp.rwolf.qmd).

```{python}
models = pf.feols("sw(Y, Y2) ~ X1 + X2", data=data)
pf.bonferroni(models, param="X1")
```

```{python}
pf.rwolf(models, param="X1", reps=99, seed=1234)
```

```{python}
pf.wyoung(models, param="X1", reps=99, seed=1234)
```

## Tables

`etable` renders models as `"gt"`, `"md"`, `"tex"`, `"typst"`, or `"df"`; see [Regression Tables](tutorials/regression-tables.qmd).

```{python}
fits = [pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2", data=data), pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1", data=data)]
pf.etable(fits, type="md", drop=["X2"])
```

```{python}
pf.etable(
    fits,
    type="md",
    keep="X1",
    labels={"X1": "Treatment", "Y": "Outcome"},
    coef_fmt="b (se) [p]",
    model_heads=["No controls", "With fixed effects"],
    head_order="hd",
)
```
